intro: Tajikistan is a mountainous country whose people speak a form of Persian and trace their roots to ancient Silk Road civilisations.

chapters.title: Sogdians and Samanids
text: Ancient Sogdiana and Bactria covered this region. Panjakent was a rich Sogdian city with painted walls.
In the 800s and 900s the Persian-speaking Samanid dynasty ruled from Bukhara, a golden age of Persian literature that Tajiks see as the start of their nation.

chapters.title: Russian and Soviet rule
text: Russia took the north in the 1860s. In 1929 Tajikistan became a full Soviet republic, but the great Tajik cities of Samarkand and Bukhara were placed in Uzbekistan.

chapters.title: Civil war and after
text: After independence in 1991 a civil war from 1992 to 1997 killed tens of thousands. Emomali Rahmon has ruled since 1992.

keyTerms.meaning: A form of the Persian language.
